Her element — osmium: a hard, brittle blue-white metal, the densest natural element at about 22.6 grams per cubic centimetre, twice as heavy as lead and rivalled only by iridium; found in 1803 together with iridium in the black residue left after platinum dissolves in aqua regia, and named from the Greek word for smell because its volatile oxide gives off a sharp, chlorine-like stench; that oxide vapour stains fats black and has long been used to reveal the shapes of cells under the microscope; its hard alloys once tipped fountain-pen nibs and gramophone needles — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.
